A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CUDA-L1 study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–B. Both have 36 pages; text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical pages 2–36, with differences confined to title-page front matter.

before.justification: v10 reports original CUDA-L1 experiments on 250 KernelBench tasks, including benchmark results, component ablations and evaluations across GPU architectures (Tables 4–6).

after.justification: v11 retains these original experiments, including the 3.12x mean A100 speedup in Table 4, component ablations in Table 5 and GPU-transfer results in Table 6.

M1.justification: The three-stage training pipeline, DeepSeek-V3 backbone, contrastive exemplar selection, GRPO objective and reward-hacking mitigations remain identical in Sections 2–3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 250 KernelBench tasks across Levels 1–3 and the same A100, RTX 3090, H100, H20 and L40 evaluation environments. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same reference-code, Torch Compile, reduce-overhead and CUDA Graph comparisons, alongside the same vanilla and evolutionary LLM comparators in Table 5.

E3.justification: The correctness checks, randomized paired timing, 30-minute training-reward measurements, 20-minute evaluation windows, metrics and 1.01x speedup threshold are unchanged (Sections 2 and 4).

E4.justification: The training-stage and exemplar-sampling ablations (Table 5), LSTM and Conv3d optimization-combination studies (Tables 8–9), reward-hacking analyses and appendix case studies are identical.

E5.justification: Repeated timing, seven-bucket variance filtering and median reward estimation in Section 2.4.4 are unchanged, as are the five attempts per vanilla baseline in Section 4.4. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the image-based Tables 8–9. For example, Table 4 retains the A100 mean speedup of 3.12x, median of 1.42x and 226/250 tasks exceeding 1.01x.

T1.justification: The definitions in Section 2.1, Equations (1)–(6) and diagonal-matrix complexity argument in Section 5.1 are identical. No mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive RL, optimization speedups, autonomous technique discovery and portability across GPU architectures.

C2.justification: Reward-hacking caveats, explanations of component effectiveness, interpretations of GPU-transfer results and optimization-mechanism discussions remain unchanged in Sections 3–5.

D1.justification: Both versions provide identical prompts, implementation and measurement details, code-access information and appendix code with hyperparameters. The repository link and its target are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and the discussions positioning CUDA-L1 relative to evolutionary LLMs and RL-based code optimization are retained, including Sections 2.4.1 and 6.

P1.justification: v11 removes Xiaofei Sun and adds Guoyin Wang in the author list, removes Xiaofei Sun's email entry, updates the arXiv version/date and reorders the abstract-end footnote markers. Other prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–16 retain identical content, formatting and placement, including appendix code displays. The title-page text edits do not alter the document's layout or displays.

improvement.justification: The revision changes only title-page author/contact information, version/date text and footnote-marker order. Methods, results, analysis, scientific exposition and Appendices A–B remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
